VIDEO.title: The SHOCKING Reason Jesus Went to the Gates of HELL
VIDEO.series: The Gospel of Matthew Every Word (playlist of 58 videos)

hand: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Matthew 16:1-20. Pharisees and Sadducees come together to test Jesus and ask for a sign from heaven. He says they can read the sky but not the signs of the times, and no sign will be given but the sign of Jonah. In the boat He warns the disciples about the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, which they finally understand is their teaching. At Caesarea Philippi He asks, 'But who do you say that I am?' Peter answers, 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.'

The two parties usually disagreed; the video compares it to Republicans and Democrats coming together. Since the Pharisees were already plotting to destroy Him (12:14), the request is not in good faith. Mark adds that He was 'sighing deeply in His spirit' (Mark 8:12).
The signs of the times are Jesus' own teaching and miracles, which were meant to deepen trust in God (Exodus 4; Isaiah 45:2-3). The sign of Jonah was already explained in chapter 12.

Location matters: Caesarea Philippi sat at the base of Mount Hermon, a site of Baal worship and later of the god Pan, which the video says the Romans understood to be the gates of hell. The keys of the kingdom recall the key of the house of David (Isaiah 22:22); binding and loosing is a Hebrew idiom the video will unpack later.

The lesson: Jesus' expectation of His holy church is that they will be aggressive warriors against all aspects of hell and its activity. To spread God's kingdom is not to remove yourself from sinners but to lean in, as Israel was meant to bless the nations and as Ezekiel's fishermen stand by the healed sea.
QUOTES: Jesus' expectation of his people, that is his holy church, is that they will be aggressive warriors against all aspects of hell and its activity.
To obey Jesus and spread God's kingdom is not to remove yourself from sinners, but to lean in.
It's not Jesus' church that is doing the prevailing. It's hell itself.

method.p: The teacher tracks Jesus' movements: He leaves the Pharisees and Sadducees (16:4), then takes His disciples to a pagan shrine before naming His church. Location is important, so read the place as part of the lesson.

LSB_QUOTES.text: And Simon Peter answered and said, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
And I also say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build My church; and the gates of Hades will not overpower it.
Then I will set the key of the house of David on his shoulder, / When he opens no one will shut, / When he shuts no one will open.

left.text: And the Pharisees and Sadducees came, and testing Him, they asked Him to show them a sign from heaven.

Since the Pharisees were already plotting to destroy Him, their request for a sign is not in good faith.

LEAVEN.title: Red skies and the signs of the times

src.text: But He replied to them, “When it is evening, you say, ‘It will be fair weather, for the sky is red.’ And in the morning, ‘There will be a storm today, for the sky is red and threatening.’ Do you know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but cannot discern the signs of the times?

lines.text: 'Signs of the times' is often used for end-times matters, but here, the video says, it simply refers to Jesus' own teaching and miracles in the first century.
Signs were given to deepen trust in God (Exodus 4, 7 and 14; Isaiah 45:2-3), 'So that you may know that it is I, / Yahweh, the God of Israel, who calls you by your name' (Isaiah 45:3).

left.text: An evil and adulterous generation eagerly seeks for a sign; and a sign will not be given it, except the sign of Jonah.” And He left them and went away.

right.text: And Yahweh appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the stomach of the fish three days and three nights.

lines.text: This is the same answer Jesus gave in Matthew 12. There He spoke of the Ninevites and the Queen of the South, who recognized what God was doing; these leaders do not.
Mark adds that He was 'sighing deeply in His spirit' (Mark 8:12). He leaves them and departs, a physical and symbolic removal of His presence from corrupt leaders.

src.text: How is it that you do not understand that I did not speak to you concerning bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.” Then they understood that He did not say to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

lines.text: 'Does this sound familiar? We just went over this.' Jesus again points to the loaves and baskets (16:9-10). Leaven is teaching that spreads through the whole lump.
Mark has 'the leaven of Herod' (Mark 8:15); Luke calls the leaven of the Pharisees 'hypocrisy' (Luke 12:1).

GATES.title: Caesarea Philippi, at the foot of Hermon

src.text: Now when Jesus came into the district of Caesarea Philippi, He was asking His disciples, saying, “Who do people say that the Son of Man is?”

lines.text: Caesarea Philippi was built by Philip the tetrarch at the base of Mount Hermon. Hermon, the video says, was a contentious site for Jews in the first century.
Luke names 'his brother Philip' as tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis (Luke 3:1). Philip rebuilt the town at the springs called Paneas and named it for Caesar.

Many believed the sons of God who desired the daughters of men (Genesis 6) descended on Mount Hermon. Canaanites and Phoenicians worshiped Baal there; after the Greeks and Romans, it became a shrine to the god Pan.

The video says the Romans understood Mount Hermon, and by extension Caesarea Philippi, to be the gates of hell. Jesus takes His disciples right to that spot to teach them about His identity and the church's purpose.
The descent on Hermon is told in 1 Enoch 6, not in Genesis. The cave and niches of Pan's shrine can still be seen at Banias.

src.text: And Simon Peter answered and said, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” And Jesus answered and said to him, “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but My Father who is in heaven. And I also say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build My church; and the gates of Hades will not overpower it.

lines.text: Notice the language: it is not Jesus' church that fails to prevail. 'Prevail' means to have the strength to withstand; it is hell itself that will not withstand the church.
Peter (Petros) and rock (petra) are a wordplay. Whether the rock is Peter, his confession, or Christ Himself has long been debated; the video does not settle it here.

left.text: And it will be that fishermen will stand beside it; from Engedi to Eneglaim there will be a place for the spreading of nets. Their fish will be according to their kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, very many.

right.text: And He *said to them, “Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men.”

lines.text: Israel was supposed to bless the nations, reclaiming them from idol worship. In Ezekiel's vision the river from the temple heals the sea, and the fish stand for the nations.
'What did Jesus call His disciples? Fishers of men.' This is a call back to Ezekiel 47.

KEYS.title: The key of the house of David

left.text: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you bind on earth shall have been bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall have been loosed in heaven.”

right.text: Then I will set the key of the house of David on his shoulder, / When he opens no one will shut, / When he shuts no one will open.

lines.text: The key in Isaiah is God-given authority to let people into the city or not. The Lord speaks of a new leader who will open and shut the gates of Jerusalem, which also stands for the city of God.
Revelation gives the risen Jesus 'the keys of death and of Hades' (Revelation 1:18).

src.text: Truly I say to you, whatever you bind on earth shall have been bound in heaven; and whatever you loose on earth shall have been loosed in heaven.

lines.text: The video calls this a Hebrew idiomatic expression and says much of what Christians say about it is incorrect. It promises to unpack it later.
Jesus repeats the words to all the disciples in 18:18. Many scholars note that later rabbinic writings use 'bind' and 'loose' for forbidding and permitting.

KEYS.title: From corrupt leaders to the gates of hell

lines.text: Picture the contrast: Yahweh's religious leaders don't know Him, so Jesus leaves them. Then He takes His disciples to the gates of hell and tells them precisely what God's people are supposed to do.
If your goal is to look clean and keep away from pagans, this is a problem. That, the video says, is why the religious leaders of the first century struggled with Jesus.
Jesus' expectation of His people, that is His holy church, is that they will be aggressive warriors against all aspects of hell and its activity.
To obey Jesus and spread God's kingdom is not to remove yourself from sinners, but to lean in, to go to sinners, and to spread the truth to all.

BACKGROUND.p: At the foot of Mount Hermon a spring flows from a cave, one of the sources of the Jordan. In the Greek period it became a shrine to Pan, with niches cut in the cliff; Herod the Great built a temple there for Augustus, and Philip the tetrarch made the town his capital, renaming it Caesarea. Its Arabic name, Banias, keeps the old name.

The Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 6) says the angels who sinned with women descended on Mount Hermon and bound themselves by oath there. The book is older than the New Testament and is echoed in Jude 14-15. Genesis 6 itself does not name the place.

The Sadducees were linked to the priestly aristocracy and the temple; the Pharisees were teachers of the oral tradition. They differed on resurrection, angels and the authority of tradition (Acts 23:8), which makes their joint approach striking.

DEBATES.h: Who or what is the rock?
DEBATES.p: Readers have taken the rock as Peter himself (as first confessor and leader), as Peter's confession of faith (Chrysostom), or as Christ. Some, with the setting in mind, add the rock face of Hermon's shrine. The wordplay Petros/petra ties the rock closely to Peter.

DEBATES.h: Gates of Hades: defense or attack?
DEBATES.p: The video reads the gates as hell's defenses that cannot withstand the church's advance. Others take 'gates of Hades' as death itself, which will not overpower the church (Isaiah 38:10).
Interpretations include declaring what is forbidden or permitted, forgiving or retaining sins (John 20:23), and church discipline (18:15-18). The video promises its own reading later.

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: 'Gates of hell' is the wording of the translation the video reads; the LSB has 'the gates of Hades' (16:18). Hades is the realm of the dead, not Gehenna.
The belief that the sons of God descended on Mount Hermon comes from 1 Enoch 6, not from Genesis 6, which does not name a place.

The claim that the Romans called Hermon 'the gates of hell' is not sourced in the video. Popular teachers often call the cave at Pan's shrine 'the gates of hell'; Josephus describes a deep cave and spring there but does not use that name.

The video says the Ninevites were 'prideful' and the Queen of the South 'didn't believe.' The queen did say 'I did not believe those words, until I came and my eyes had seen it' (1 Kings 10:7); Jesus' point in 12:41-42 is that both responded.
Philip did not found the town from nothing: he rebuilt Paneas at the springs and renamed it.
The captions write 'Cesaria Philippi,' 'Barjonah,' 'Bahal' and 'Bal' for Baal, 'levan' for leaven, and 'esqueological' for eschatological.

QUESTIONS: Why do you think the Pharisees and Sadducees, usual rivals, joined forces here?
The disciples missed the point about leaven. What teaching quietly shapes you without your noticing?
Who do people today say Jesus is? Who do you say He is?
Why might Jesus have chosen a pagan shrine for this conversation?
What does it mean for you to 'lean in' to sinners rather than withdraw?
Where do you see the gates of Hades giving way in your community?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: The lesson, stated plainly: Jesus' expectation of His people, that is His holy church, is that they will be aggressive warriors against all aspects of hell and its activity. In other words, to obey Jesus and spread God's kingdom is not to remove yourself from sinners, but to lean in, to go to sinners, and to spread the truth to all. That caused a problem for the religious leaders of the first century, whose goal was to look clean and keep away. Israel was meant to bless the nations, reclaiming them from false worship; Ezekiel saw fishermen beside a healed sea, and Jesus made His disciples fishers of men. So He leaves the corrupt leaders, takes His disciples to the gates of hell, and tells them precisely what God's people are supposed to do.
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): write out Peter's confession (16:16) in your own words. Then name one 'dark place' in your town, a person or a setting you tend to avoid, and one concrete way to bring Christ's truth and kindness there this month.

   Location Matthew 16:13: "Now when Jesus came into the district of Caesarea Philippi, He was asking His disciples, saying, “Who do people say that the Son of Man is?”" https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+16:13
   (video) Caesarea Philippi was built by Philip the tetrarch at the base of Mount Hermon. Hermon, the video says, was a contentious site for Jews in the first century.
   [Background] Luke names 'his brother Philip' as tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis (Luke 3:1). Philip rebuilt the town at the springs called Paneas and named it for Caesar. (Luke 3:1)
2. Hermon's dark history: Baal, then Pan
   (video) Many believed the sons of God who desired the daughters of men (Genesis 6) descended on Mount Hermon. Canaanites and Phoenicians worshiped Baal there; after the Greeks and Romans, it became a shrine to the god Pan.
   (video) The video says the Romans understood Mount Hermon, and by extension Caesarea Philippi, to be the gates of hell. Jesus takes His disciples right to that spot to teach them about His identity and the church's purpose.
   [Background] The descent on Hermon is told in 1 Enoch 6, not in Genesis. The cave and niches of Pan's shrine can still be seen at Banias.
3. Matthew 16:15-18: You are the Christ
   Confession Matthew 16:16-18: "And Simon Peter answered and said, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” And Jesus answered and said to him, “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but My Father who is in heaven. And I also say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build My church; and the gates of Hades will not overpower it." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+16:16-18
   (video) Notice the language: it is not Jesus' church that fails to prevail. 'Prevail' means to have the strength to withstand; it is hell itself that will not withstand the church.
   [Background] Peter (Petros) and rock (petra) are a wordplay. Whether the rock is Peter, his confession, or Christ Himself has long been debated; the video does not settle it here.
4. Ezekiel 47:9-10; Matthew 4:19: Fishermen by the healed sea
   Ezekiel (Ezekiel 47:10, LSB): "And it will be that fishermen will stand beside it; from Engedi to Eneglaim there will be a place for the spreading of nets. Their fish will be according to their kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, very many."
   Jesus (Matthew 4:19, LSB): "And He *said to them, “Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men.”"
   (video) Israel was supposed to bless the nations, reclaiming them from idol worship. In Ezekiel's vision the river from the temple heals the sea, and the fish stand for the nations.
   (video) 'What did Jesus call His disciples? Fishers of men.' This is a call back to Ezekiel 47.

## The keys of the kingdom
1. Matthew 16:19; Isaiah 22:22: The key of the house of David
   Jesus (Matthew 16:19, LSB): "I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you bind on earth shall have been bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall have been loosed in heaven.”"
   Isaiah (Isaiah 22:22, LSB): "Then I will set the key of the house of David on his shoulder, / When he opens no one will shut, / When he shuts no one will open."
   (video) The key in Isaiah is God-given authority to let people into the city or not. The Lord speaks of a new leader who will open and shut the gates of Jerusalem, which also stands for the city of God.
   [Background] Revelation gives the risen Jesus 'the keys of death and of Hades' (Revelation 1:18). (Revelation 1:18)
2. Matthew 16:19; 18:18: Binding and loosing
   Idiom Matthew 18:18: "Truly I say to you, whatever you bind on earth shall have been bound in heaven; and whatever you loose on earth shall have been loosed in heaven." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+18:18
   (video) The video calls this a Hebrew idiomatic expression and says much of what Christians say about it is incorrect. It promises to unpack it later.
   [Background] Jesus repeats the words to all the disciples in 18:18. Many scholars note that later rabbinic writings use 'bind' and 'loose' for forbidding and permitting.
3. Matthew 16:4, 13: From corrupt leaders to the gates of hell
   (video) Picture the contrast: Yahweh's religious leaders don't know Him, so Jesus leaves them. Then He takes His disciples to the gates of hell and tells them precisely what God's people are supposed to do.
   (video) If your goal is to look clean and keep away from pagans, this is a problem. That, the video says, is why the religious leaders of the first century struggled with Jesus.
4. The lesson: Aggressive warriors against hell
   (video) Jesus' expectation of His people, that is His holy church, is that they will be aggressive warriors against all aspects of hell and its activity.
   (video) To obey Jesus and spread God's kingdom is not to remove yourself from sinners, but to lean in, to go to sinners, and to spread the truth to all.

## Key people
- Pharisees and Sadducees: Usual rivals, united in testing Jesus for a sign. [Background] The Sadducees denied the resurrection; the Pharisees held to it (Acts 23:8).
- Simon Peter: Confesses, 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.' [Background] Jesus had named him Cephas, 'which is translated Peter' (John 1:42).
- Jonah: His three days in the fish is the only sign given. [Background] Jesus explained the sign in 12:40.
- Philip the tetrarch: Built Caesarea Philippi at the base of Mount Hermon. [Background] A son of Herod the Great; tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis (Luke 3:1).
- John the Baptist, Elijah, Jeremiah: Who people said the Son of Man was. [Background] Herod also thought Jesus was John risen (14:2).

## Places [Background]
- Caesarea Philippi (named in the video): Where Peter confesses Jesus (16:13); the captions write 'Cesaria Philippi.' Today Banias.
- Mount Hermon (named in the video): The high mountain above Caesarea Philippi, linked with Baal worship.
- Magadan: Where the boat landed before the Pharisees came (15:39).
- Bethsaida: Mark has the boat cross to Bethsaida after the warning about leaven (Mark 8:22).

## Key terms
- Sign from heaven: A proof from God on demand; Jesus refuses to perform one for those testing Him.
- Signs of the times: Here, Jesus' own teaching and miracles, which showed what God was doing.
- Leaven: Yeast; here the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees (16:12). The captions write 'levan.'
- Caesarea Philippi: Philip's city at the springs below Mount Hermon, also called Paneas; today Banias.
- Gates of Hades: The LSB wording of 16:18; the video, reading another translation, says 'gates of hell.'
- Keys of the kingdom: Authority to open and shut, recalling the key of David (Isaiah 22:22).
- Binding and loosing: A Hebrew idiom, the video says; often read as forbidding and permitting.
- Church: Greek ekklēsia, an assembly; Jesus' people gathered around Him. [Background]

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Paneas and Pan: At the foot of Mount Hermon a spring flows from a cave, one of the sources of the Jordan. In the Greek period it became a shrine to Pan, with niches cut in the cliff; Herod the Great built a temple there for Augustus, and Philip the tetrarch made the town his capital, renaming it Caesarea. Its Arabic name, Banias, keeps the old name.
- Hermon in 1 Enoch: The Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 6) says the angels who sinned with women descended on Mount Hermon and bound themselves by oath there. The book is older than the New Testament and is echoed in Jude 14-15. Genesis 6 itself does not name the place.
- Pharisees and Sadducees: The Sadducees were linked to the priestly aristocracy and the temple; the Pharisees were teachers of the oral tradition. They differed on resurrection, angels and the authority of tradition (Acts 23:8), which makes their joint approach striking.

## Early witnesses [Background: sourced]
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "And why said He not plainly, Beware of their teaching? His will is to remind them of what had been done, for He knew they had forgotten." Homilies on Matthew 53, on 16:5-6. Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 10 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "leading them far away from the Jews, so that being freed from all alarm, they might speak with boldness all that was in their mind." Homilies on Matthew 54, on 16:13. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "upon this rock will I build my Church; … that is, on the faith of his confession." Homilies on Matthew 54, on 16:18. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Who or what is the rock? Readers have taken the rock as Peter himself (as first confessor and leader), as Peter's confession of faith (Chrysostom), or as Christ. Some, with the setting in mind, add the rock face of Hermon's shrine. The wordplay Petros/petra ties the rock closely to Peter.
- Gates of Hades: defense or attack? The video reads the gates as hell's defenses that cannot withstand the church's advance. Others take 'gates of Hades' as death itself, which will not overpower the church (Isaiah 38:10).
- Binding and loosing Interpretations include declaring what is forbidden or permitted, forgiving or retaining sins (John 20:23), and church discipline (18:15-18). The video promises its own reading later.

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- 'Gates of hell' is the wording of the translation the video reads; the LSB has 'the gates of Hades' (16:18). Hades is the realm of the dead, not Gehenna.
- The belief that the sons of God descended on Mount Hermon comes from 1 Enoch 6, not from Genesis 6, which does not name a place.
- The claim that the Romans called Hermon 'the gates of hell' is not sourced in the video. Popular teachers often call the cave at Pan's shrine 'the gates of hell'; Josephus describes a deep cave and spring there but does not use that name.
- The video says the Ninevites were 'prideful' and the Queen of the South 'didn't believe.' The queen did say 'I did not believe those words, until I came and my eyes had seen it' (1 Kings 10:7); Jesus' point in 12:41-42 is that both responded.
- Philip did not found the town from nothing: he rebuilt Paneas at the springs and renamed it.
- The captions write 'Cesaria Philippi,' 'Barjonah,' 'Bahal' and 'Bal' for Baal, 'levan' for leaven, and 'esqueological' for eschatological.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. Why do you think the Pharisees and Sadducees, usual rivals, joined forces here?
2. The disciples missed the point about leaven. What teaching quietly shapes you without your noticing?
3. Who do people today say Jesus is? Who do you say He is?
4. Why might Jesus have chosen a pagan shrine for this conversation?
5. What does it mean for you to 'lean in' to sinners rather than withdraw?
6. Where do you see the gates of Hades giving way in your community?

## Application
- (video) The lesson, stated plainly: Jesus' expectation of His people, that is His holy church, is that they will be aggressive warriors against all aspects of hell and its activity. In other words, to obey Jesus and spread God's kingdom is not to remove yourself from sinners, but to lean in, to go to sinners, and to spread the truth to all. That caused a problem for the religious leaders of the first century, whose goal was to look clean and keep away. Israel was meant to bless the nations, reclaiming them from false worship; Ezekiel saw fishermen beside a healed sea, and Jesus made His disciples fishers of men. So He leaves the corrupt leaders, takes His disciples to the gates of hell, and tells them precisely what God's people are supposed to do.
- Study note (added): write out Peter's confession (16:16) in your own words. Then name one 'dark place' in your town, a person or a setting you tend to avoid, and one concrete way to bring Christ's truth and kindness there this month.
